text: latex-look 是一款面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 LaTeX 页面检查插件，通过注册 latex_look 工具，让 agent 编译文档、把指定 PDF 页面渲染为 PNG，并将页面文字或坐标定位回源文件行。它还能把当前页面与先前 PDF 并排比较、检查全书新增的版面问题，以及核对图表标签的阅读顺序；返回内容包括构建问题、警告、定位结果和图像路径。适合需要根据实际排版效果修改论文、书稿或其他 TeX 文档，并在修改后确认变化的用户。运行需要 Node.js 18 以上，以及 TeX 引擎、SyncTeX 和 Ghostscript。

latex-look adds a latex_look tool to DeepSeek Harness. It compiles TeX, renders PDF pages as PNG, maps text or coordinates to source lines, compares pages, and checks layout or label order. For visual verification of paper and book edits. Requires Node.js 18+, a TeX engine, SyncTeX, and Ghostscript.
想让 agent 看见 LaTeX 编译出来的页面实际长什么样。
修改论文排版后，怎么对照前后 PDF 找出具体变化？
I need to map a visible spot in a rendered TeX page back to its source line.
latex-look 的功能「渲染并定位页面」：调用 latex_look 编译主 .tex 文件，将指定页输出为 PNG；还可按页面文字或 PDF 坐标定位对应的源文件和行。
latex-look 的功能「比较版面并检查整书」：调用 latex_look 并提供之前的 PDF，可获得前后页面并排图像；也可运行全页审查或检查图表标签的阅读顺序。
latex-look 会向 registry.npmjs.org 查询该插件的 latest 版本，以显示更新提示；源码中的查询只请求版本信息，不包含用户的 LaTeX 文档。（见 lib/update.mjs:149-153）

text:
@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · latex-look — teach an agent to *see* your LaTeX：A **DeepSeek Harness plugin** that adds exactly one tool: `latex_look`.

An agent that only reads `.tex` source is blind: a document can compile with zero errors and still look wrong. `latex_look` compiles the document, renders the page as an image, maps any spot on that page back to the exact source line, and diffs what your last edit changed — in a single call.
section: latex-look — teach an agent to *see* your LaTeX

text:
@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · latex-look — teach an agent to *see* your LaTeX：```
        ┌─────────────┐   latex_look   ┌──────────────┐
        │   agent     │ ─────────────► │  pdf → png   │
        │ (edits .tex)│                │  synctex     │
        └─────────────┘ ◄───────────── │  pixel diff  │

**Read the case study:** [a 215-page LaTeX book, read the way a reader reads it](CASE-STUDY.md) — 163 figures, 129 equations, six classes of defect that compile cleanly.
section: latex-look — teach an agent to *see* your LaTeX

text:
@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Why one tool, not three：Rendering, locating, and diffing are the *implementation*. The agent needs one coherent verb — **"look at this page"** — the same way a person does. `latex_look` compiles, renders, resolves, and diffs in a single call, so the loop is:

```
look → diagnose → edit .tex → look again → confirm the change → report
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Install：Requires Node ≥ 18, a TeX engine (`xelatex`/`lualatex`/`pdflatex`/`latexmk` or tectonic), `synctex`, and `ghostscript`.

This repository **is** the bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fangchenghao/latex-look
```

Then install it into the current profile (in the Harness, via the plugin manager):

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: /absolute/path/to/latex-look
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Install：That adds the row `latex-look` and registers the `latex_look` tool. Replacing the sources of an already-installed package needs a Harness restart to load a fresh module generation.

Published on npm as [`@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look), so the same row also installs straight from the registry:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: @fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Updating：Two different facts, and the plugin reports them separately because confusing them is
how an update goes missing:

**A newer release exists.** The registry is asked once a day, in the background; when
something newer is published, one line is appended to a tool reply. An offline machine
sees nothing at all, and an unreachable registry is never reported as "up to date".

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Updating：**A newer release is already installed.** This is the one that silently bites. An
updater replaces the package directory while the old code keeps running, so the
running code goes on reading its version out of a `package.json` that was swapped
underneath it — it reports the *new* number while executing the *old* code, and
everything looks current. The plugin therefore remembers the version it started with,
re-reads the disk at most once a minute, and when the two disagree says so:

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Updating：```
note: @fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look 0.4.2 is installed on disk, but this process is
still running 0.4.1 — restart DeepSeek Harness to load it.
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Updating：The plugin does not update itself. Replacing the files of a running process is the
profile's job, not a tool's: an updater plugin already installed in the profile does
it, or you do it by hand. When the plugin can tell which profile it was installed
into, it prints the exact command — the profile name is read off its own path,
because they are called `desktop` and `web` and a guess sends you to an install that
does nothing:

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Updating：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look@latest
```

`core.mjs` is not hot-reloaded, so a plugin update takes effect on the next start of
the harness, never mid-session.

From a checkout, both questions are available directly:

```bash
node bin/latex-look.mjs --version
node bin/latex-look.mjs --check-update
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Releasing：Tagging `v*` runs the test suite on Ubuntu with TeX and Ghostscript installed, verifies the tag matches `package.json`, and publishes to npm. The token comes from the `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Optional: the knowledge skill：The tool gives the agent eyes. [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) gives it the LaTeX knowledge to act on what it sees — a symptom → cause → fix playbook (a rule you want gone is usually `\pagestyle`/`fancyhdr`, not a stray `\hline`). Copy or symlink it into the skills root:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills/latex-look
ln -sf "$PWD/SKILL.md" ~/.dsh/skills/latex-look/SKILL.md
```

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · CLI, for humans and for testing：```bash
node bin/latex-look.mjs book.tex --page 37
node bin/latex-look.mjs book.tex --text "表3.1"
node bin/latex-look.mjs book.tex --page 12 --compare previous --json
node bin/latex-look.mjs book.tex --page 1 --audit   # what did the last edit break, anywhere?

The CLI runs the same engine as the plugin and needs no Harness, which makes it the fast way to check a change without reloading anything.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Tests：Three suites run on a clean checkout — they create their own fixtures and compile
real documents, so expect a few minutes:

```bash
node test/smoke.mjs           # unit level: problem parsing, PPM, raster diff, aux detection
node test/scenarios.mjs       # 52 end-to-end cases driven through index.js
node test/scenarios-deep.mjs  # 29 cases: multi-file papers, beamer, twocolumn, images,
                              #   engine switching, the build cache, hostile inputs

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Tests：The book suite needs a real book and is skipped unless you point it at one:

```bash
LATEX_LOOK_BOOK=/path/to/book node test/book-scenarios.mjs
```

These two suites matter most, because a real book is root → `\input{main}` →
`\input{chap1}`, with a custom `.sty`, 181 figures, a glossary and `fancyhdr` page
furniture.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Tests：`book-scenarios` checks the machinery on that book. `book-tasks` checks the
*requests*: each case is a sentence a user would say, applied to the copy and then
verified the way an agent verifies it — look, diff against the previous build, and
confirm the change is where the edit acts:

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Tests：| user says | measured |
|---|---|
| 把页眉那条横线去掉 | `0.09%`, bbox `y=52 h=1` (a thin band at the top) |
| 页眉的线太细，加粗到 2pt | `0.27%`, bbox `y=52 h=3` |
| 链接的蓝色去掉 | `0.29%`, bbox over the contents page |
| 行距调大一点 | `10.53%`, 208 → 248 pages |
| 表格行距加大 | `9.07%` |
| chap2 那个总结框太窄，放宽 | `7.39%` |
| chap1 那个图太小，放大 | `10.57%` |
| chap4 那组图对齐时右边空着 | `8.81%` |
| 段落首行不要缩进 | `14.07%` |
| 页边距太窄 | `13.32%`, 208 → 226 pages |
| 正文字号改成 12pt | `11.63%`, 208 → 226 pages |
| 目录只显示到章 | `2.19%`, 208 → 207 pages |

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Tests：Both end-to-end suites stub only `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (it exists solely inside
the Harness) and call the real `execute` with real arguments, so they exercise the
argument handling and the exact text the model reads — not just `lib/core.mjs`.
That matters: several bugs found this way lived only in the formatting layer.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · The page SyncTeX names is not always the page it is on：SyncTeX records the page a box was **built** on. A float that TeX moves to the next
page gets the previous page's number, so `text: "Version 0.5"` used to answer
"page 205" for a table that ships on 206 — and page 205 is a different chapter.
The tool now checks the PDF's own text layer (`gs -sDEVICE=txtwrite`, ~0.12 s a page)
and looks one and two pages either side; when it overrules SyncTeX it says so.
section: The page SyncTeX names is not always the page it is on

text:
@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · One picture, not two：A `compare` call writes three images, but the one to show the user is
`images.sideBySide`: the page before on the left, the page after on the right, one
PNG. Finding the difference by eye across two separate files is the hardest part of
the job for someone who cannot read the source.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Performance：Verifying an edit always costs a real compile; there is no way around that. But
browsing pages of the same build should not:

| operation | 208-page book |
|---|---|
| first look (3 passes + glossary) | ~17 s |
| every look after that, sources unchanged | ~0.2 s |

A build is reused when the document, everything it `\input`/`\include`s (three
levels), its `\includegraphics` files and its aux files are unchanged (mtime and
size). A failing build is never reused. Pass `fresh: true` to bypass it.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Performance：- **The before-snapshot belongs to the build, not to the call.** After an edit, the
  first look records what the page looked like before it; every later look at that
  same build reuses the same snapshot, so an agent inspecting three pages of its
  own edit still sees a diff on the second and third. (It used to be consumed by
  the first call, which is exactly the wrong way round.)
- **One build per document at a time.** Two compiles of the same file share its
  `.aux`/`.toc` and corrupt each other — racing two processes on the 208-page book,
  one of them died with no error message at all. Builds are now serialised in-process
  by a promise queue and across processes by a lock file that carries the owner's
  PID, so a killed run cannot wedge the document.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Performance：`-draftmode` on the intermediate passes was measured and rejected: it saves about
2%, because the time is typesetting, not PDF writing. The ~16 s is TeX itself.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · The tool：- compile status, pass count, page count, and structured `problems` — each with `file`, `line`, `message`
- `warnings`: LaTeX/Package/Class warnings plus **Overfull/Underfull** boxes, the usual cause of an ugly page
- `toc`: whether the document declares `\tableofcontents` and how many entries it actually produced (an empty TOC is reported as a problem, not a success). The declaration is found across `\input`/`\include`, so a one-line root that wraps `\input{main}` still works
- `aux`: external tools it ran — `makeglossaries`, `makeindex`, `biber`, `bibtex` — chosen from the artifacts the first pass produced, not from the root file's text, so multi-file projects that keep `\makeglossaries` in an included preamble are handled too
- PNG path(s) for the rendered page — hand these to an image reader
- `located`: `{ file, line, page }` for the text anchor or point you asked about
- `diff`: `changedRatio` plus the bounding box of the change **in PDF points**, ready to feed back into `pointX`/`pointY`
- `sequence`: reading order of labels that start a line ("图 1-1", "Figure 3.2", …). A float is placed later than an inline object that follow

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · How the locating works：`latex_look` compiles with `-synctex=1`, so every glyph carries a link to its source line. Then:

- **point → source**: `synctex edit -o page:x:y:file.pdf`
- **text → source**: search the `.tex` sources for the string, then `synctex view` each hit to get its page and coordinates
- **diff bbox → source**: pass the bbox centre as `pointX`/`pointY`

Coordinates are PDF points (72/inch) with the origin at the **top-left** of the page.

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · Honest limits：- **`page` is the PDF page index, not the number printed on the page.** In the test
  book those differ by 10 (printed 130 = index 140), and the offset is different again
  in the roman-numbered front matter. PDF page labels would let the tool translate, but
  LaTeX only writes them on request, so an agent that takes a page number from a user
  must confirm it against the rendered page first.
- SyncTeX resolves to the *nearest text position*. A decorative rule drawn by a page style (`\pagestyle{headings}`, `fancyhdr`) has no glyph of its own, so it resolves to nearby text. Combine the coordinates with LaTeX knowledge — that is what `SKILL.md` is for.
- Multi-pass convergence is checked by hashing `.aux`/`.toc`/`.out`/… — a document with `\tableofcontents` needs ≥ 2 passes, and `latex_look` reports a problem if the TOC comes out empty.
- Multi-file detection follows `\input`/`\include` three levels deep. `\import`/`\subfile`, unusual custom `.latexmkrc` recipes, and `\includeonly` are not understood.
- Cross-engine pixel parity is impossible: TeX vs Word, or two different TeX engines, have different line-breaking engines. This to

section: latex-look — 让 Agent 真正「看见」你的 LaTeX

text:
@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · 它解决什么问题：一个只会读 `.tex` 源码的 Agent 是**瞎的**。

文档可以编译零错误、打开正常，但读者一眼就看出不对：这页最上面多了一条横线、这个表格丑、
这段文字压到了页边、图太大了、两页之间空了一大块、图号怎么从 3-4 跳回 3-3 了……
这些**没有一条是编译错误**，`grep` 也搜不到——那条横线根本不在源码里，它是宏包画的。

这类需求你只能这样表达：

> 「把这一页最上面的横线去掉」「这个表格改成三线表」「图小一点」
> 「这两页之间空太多了，填满」「图号顺序不对」

`latex_look` 就是让 Agent 接得住这些话：**编译 → 渲染成图 → 定位到源码行 → 改完再比一次**，
一个调用做完。Agent 于是能进入 `看 → 诊断 → 改 → 再看 → 确认` 的循环，而不是改完就说「应该好了」。

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · 三个能力，一个动词：| 你说的话 | 它做什么 |
|---|---|
| 「这页最上方的横线去掉」 | 渲染该页，把那条线**定位到源码行**（`fancyhdr` 的 `\headrulewidth`，或某个 `\rule`） |
| 「表格改成三线表」 | 改完渲染，用**像素 diff** 告诉你只动了表格、没碰正文 |
| 「图号顺序不对」 | 扫全书**阅读顺序**，直接列出 `图 3-4 (p63) → 图 3-3 (p64)` |
| 「这次改动有没有弄坏别处」 | 全书 `audit`：只报**这一次**新造成的版面问题，并点名是哪个图把页面顶走的 |

@fffangchenghao/dsh-latex-look README · 三个能力，一个动词：```bash
latex-look main.tex --page 62                    # 渲染第 62 页
latex-look main.tex --page 62 --at "图 3-1"       # 定位到源码行
latex-look main.tex --page 62 --compare           # 与上一版并排对比
latex-look main.tex --page 1  --sequence 图       # 检查图号阅读顺序

section: 这不是「AI 帮你写 LaTeX」
